account:
Today has mostly followed my appointment schedule: I inspected the mill's grain stall, kept lunch at home, returned for council letters, visited our neighbour for tea, and am now holding office hours. The mill stall contained 76 hay bales offered at two emeralds each. No council correspondence or other business has reached the secretary.

The unusual feature is a repeated, vague report of a 'bridge or port change at bakery.' Townspeople named baker, freight, innkeeper, builder and neighbour in varying versions; one report mentioned the innkeeper carrying a sack of bread. I have not witnessed an alteration. The secretary reports that the baker expressly denied witnessing one and said he merely handled wheat and bread with freight and the innkeeper yesterday. The secretary has not found those other two for firsthand accounts. Ordinary grain and bread deliveries may explain the activity, but I cannot establish what prompted the rumour or whether any change occurred.

There is also a small scheduling discrepancy. This morning I read an Appointment Addendum recording an eighteen o'clock ordinary town-hall meeting with our neighbour, accepted during yesterday's tea. The neighbour has confirmed the meeting and says no preparation or urgent business is needed. The secretary nevertheless just said their copy lacked it. I explained the addendum and confirmed the location, attendees and ordinary purpose. I then saw the secretary take a written book from the appointments chest and return one, though I have not read what they changed. Our neighbour is now nearby. I intend to keep the meeting and return home at nineteen. I have no evidence that the meeting or the scheduling discrepancy is connected with the bakery rumour.
